To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the apical stem of epsilon is capped by a tri-loop with two pyrimidines bulged out, and that this fold is conserved in all HBV strains.

(i) the apical stem of epsilon folds into a tri-loop closed by two C-G base pairs; (ii) the tri-loop is flanked by two unpaired pyrmidines, one bulged out and the other intercalated into its stem; (iii) this fold is highly conserved among all HBV genotypes and (iv) the NMR data are in agreement with the mutational data.
the apical stem-Loop of the HBV encapsidation signal epsilon folds into a stable Tri-loop with two underlying Pyrimidine Bulges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the encapsidation signal of the hepatitis B viral pregenomic RNA, which is the template for the synthesis of the viral DNA during reverse transcription.
the structure of the apical stem of the encapsidation signal of HBV.
the structure of the apical stem- and tri-loop of the HBV epsilon signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epsilon stem-loop fold is highly conserved and that it is the same for all genotypes.
epsilon is a highly conserved bulged stem-loop, capped by a tri-loop with two pyrimidine bulge bases, and that this fold is required for the first step in the reverse transcription of the pregenome.
epsilon folds into a stem-loop with an unpaired U at position 1889 and a bulged out pyrimidine at position 1882.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the structure of the apical stem of epsilon by NMR and that the structure is highly conserved in the HBV strains.
we show a new and more stable fold for this stem-loop than previously described and that this is essential for recognition of the pregenome by the reverse transcriptas.
the epsilon apical stem-loop is not a bulged stem capped by a 6 nt loop, but a tri-loop closed by an apical C-G base pair.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the apical stem of epsilon as a novel tri-loop fold.
a tri-loop with two unpaired pyrmidines is a stable fold.
the HBV encapsidation signal epsilon has a novel fold with a tri-loop and two underlying pyrimidines.
